title: Disentangling the percepts of illusory movement and sensory stimulation during tendon vibration in the EEG
description: EEG recordings from 20 healthy right-handed adults during tendon vibration of the left elbow, used to separate the neural correlates of illusory movement from those of plain sensory stimulation. Sixteen sensorimotor electrodes were recorded while biceps and triceps tendon vibration either induced an illusion of elbow extension or, in a control condition, produced vibration sensation alone.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with a g.tec Nautilus wireless amplifier (16 electrodes, 10-10 system, 500 Hz, 0.1-100 Hz hardware bandpass, right earlobe reference). Vibrators (Vibramoov) were placed on the distal biceps and triceps tendons of the left arm. The illusion condition used 90 Hz on biceps and 50 Hz on triceps, and the control used 70 Hz on both. Each 3 s stimulation had a 1 s ramp-up, 1 s stable interval and 1 s ramp-down. Each participant completed three blocks of 72 randomized vibrations (36 illusion, 36 control), with inter-stimulus intervals of 1-3 s.
